verdict.rationale: cubic documents an org-level config mechanism: a `cubic-config` repository in the organization holding a `cubic.yaml`, alongside per-repo `cubic.yaml` files that control review behavior, ignore patterns, and custom agents. Custom agents also enforce organization-wide practices. The evidence does not say how org defaults cascade to repos, how per-repo exceptions are declared or overridden centrally, or whether this works at a scale of hundreds of repos. missing for 10: documented inheritance/override semantics between org and repo config, central exception management, evidence of rollout at scale across many repos, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering lead, I roll out org-level review defaults across hundreds of repos and manage exceptions centrally

citations.quote: Create a repository named `cubic-config` in your organization and add a `cubic.yaml` file to the root directory.
`cubic.yaml` lives in the root of your repository and becomes the source of truth for AI review behavior, ignore patterns, PR descriptions, and custom agents.
Custom agents are review rules that enforce your organization's specific best practices across pull requests.
